requirements.title: Policies for information security
requirements.text: Maintain a current information security policy approved at management level. Evidence: signed policy, approval record, and review date.

requirements.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
requirements.text: Define security roles and assign responsibilities across the organization, including deputies. Evidence: role matrix, job descriptions, and appointment records.

requirements.title: Segregation of duties
requirements.text: Separate conflicting duties so one person cannot both initiate and approve a sensitive action. Evidence: role matrix and access review records.

requirements.title: Management responsibilities
requirements.text: Require staff to apply the information security policy and hold managers accountable for compliance in their area. Evidence: management communications and performance objectives.

requirements.title: Contact with authorities
requirements.text: Keep current contacts for regulators, law enforcement, and incident response bodies. Evidence: contact list and records of past notifications.

requirements.title: Contact with special interest groups
requirements.text: Maintain memberships and contacts with security communities and industry groups. Evidence: membership records and meeting notes.

requirements.title: Threat intelligence
requirements.text: Collect and use threat intelligence to inform risk decisions and control priorities. Evidence: threat reports, subscriptions, and action logs.

requirements.title: Information security in project management
requirements.text: Integrate information security requirements into project planning and delivery gates. Evidence: project charters, risk assessments, and gate reviews.

requirements.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
requirements.text: Keep an inventory of information and related assets with named owners. Evidence: asset register, ownership field, and periodic reconciliation.

requirements.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
requirements.text: Publish rules for acceptable use of information and assets and confirm that staff acknowledge them. Evidence: acceptable use policy and acknowledgements.

requirements.title: Return of assets
requirements.text: Require return of assets when employment or a contract ends. Evidence: exit checklists and asset return receipts.

requirements.title: Classification of information
requirements.text: Classify information by sensitivity and handling needs, and keep the scheme current. Evidence: classification policy, scheme, and tagged assets.

requirements.title: Labelling of information
requirements.text: Apply consistent labels so users can recognize sensitivity and handling rules. Evidence: labelling standard and examples from systems.

requirements.title: Information transfer
requirements.text: Protect information in transit through approved channels, agreements, and transfer rules. Evidence: transfer procedures and secure channel configuration.

requirements.title: Access control
requirements.text: Define access control rules based on business and security requirements. Evidence: access control policy and authorization records.

requirements.title: Identity management
requirements.text: Manage identities through a controlled lifecycle from creation to removal. Evidence: identity register and joiner, mover, and leaver records.

requirements.title: Authentication information
requirements.text: Control issuance, storage, and rotation of authentication secrets. Evidence: password policy, multi-factor configuration, and secret rotation logs.

requirements.title: Access rights
requirements.text: Grant, review, and revoke access rights according to approved roles and least privilege. Evidence: access approvals and periodic review reports.

requirements.title: Information security in supplier relationships
requirements.text: Assess security risks in supplier relationships before and during the engagement. Evidence: supplier risk assessments and due diligence records.

requirements.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
requirements.text: Include information security duties and expectations in supplier agreements. Evidence: contract clauses, security schedules, and signed agreements.

requirements.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
requirements.text: Manage ICT supply chain risks, including sub-suppliers and component provenance. Evidence: supply chain map, supplier attestations, and review notes.

requirements.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
requirements.text: Monitor supplier service performance and security changes, and review them periodically. Evidence: service reports, change notices, and review minutes.

requirements.title: Information security for use of cloud services
requirements.text: Define security requirements and responsibilities for cloud service use. Evidence: cloud inventory, provider contracts, and configuration reviews.

requirements.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
requirements.text: Plan and prepare incident management, including roles, channels, and escalation paths. Evidence: incident plan, contact list, and exercise records.

requirements.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
requirements.text: Triage security events consistently and record the decision to escalate or close them. Evidence: triage records and event classification criteria.

requirements.title: Response to information security incidents
requirements.text: Respond to incidents through the documented process and preserve the response record. Evidence: incident tickets, timelines, and closure reports.

requirements.title: Learning from information security incidents
requirements.text: Review incidents to identify root causes and improve controls. Evidence: post-incident reviews and tracked corrective actions.

requirements.title: Collection of evidence
requirements.text: Collect and preserve incident evidence using defensible methods. Evidence: evidence register, chain of custody, and hash records.

requirements.title: Information security during disruption
requirements.text: Keep security controls operating during disruption and document degraded-mode procedures. Evidence: continuity plan and disruption test results.

requirements.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
requirements.text: Define and test ICT recovery capability against agreed objectives. Evidence: recovery plan, recovery targets, and exercise reports.

requirements.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
requirements.text: Identify and track legal, regulatory, and contractual security obligations. Evidence: obligations register, legal review, and compliance calendar.

requirements.title: Intellectual property rights
requirements.text: Protect intellectual property and ensure software licences are used lawfully. Evidence: licence inventory and software asset records.

requirements.title: Protection of records
requirements.text: Protect records from loss, alteration, and unauthorized access for the required period. Evidence: retention schedule and storage controls.

requirements.title: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
requirements.text: Identify and protect personal data in line with privacy obligations. Evidence: data inventory, privacy notices, and handling procedures.

requirements.title: Independent review of information security
requirements.text: Obtain independent review of the security management system at planned intervals. Evidence: audit reports and management responses.

requirements.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
requirements.text: Review compliance with internal security rules and record exceptions. Evidence: compliance checks, exception register, and remediation plans.

requirements.title: Documented operating procedures
requirements.text: Document operating procedures for security-relevant tasks and keep them available to staff. Evidence: procedure library, version history, and acknowledgements.

requirements.title: Screening
requirements.text: Screen candidates before employment and repeat checks where the role requires it. Evidence: screening policy and completed check records.

requirements.title: Terms and conditions of employment
requirements.text: State security responsibilities and confidentiality duties in employment terms. Evidence: employment contracts and role descriptions.

requirements.title: Information security awareness, education and training
requirements.text: Provide role-appropriate security awareness and training, and track completion. Evidence: training plan, attendance, and assessment results.

requirements.title: Disciplinary process
requirements.text: Apply a documented disciplinary process for security policy violations. Evidence: disciplinary procedure, case records, and HR notifications.

requirements.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
requirements.text: Define security duties that continue or end when employment changes or terminates. Evidence: exit procedure and acknowledgement records.

requirements.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
requirements.text: Use confidentiality agreements that cover employees, contractors, and relevant third parties. Evidence: signed agreements and contract templates.

requirements.title: Remote working
requirements.text: Set security requirements for remote work, including devices, networks, and physical privacy. Evidence: remote work policy and device compliance reports.

requirements.title: Information security event reporting
requirements.text: Give staff a simple route to report security events and confirm that reports are handled. Evidence: reporting channel, awareness material, and report log.

requirements.title: Physical security perimeters
requirements.text: Define physical security perimeters that protect information processing facilities. Evidence: site plan, perimeter controls, and inspection records.

requirements.title: Physical entry
requirements.text: Control entry to secure areas through badges, reception, or other approved mechanisms. Evidence: access logs, visitor records, and entry procedures.

requirements.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
requirements.text: Design and protect offices, rooms, and facilities against unauthorized access and damage. Evidence: facility standards, risk assessments, and inspection reports.

requirements.title: Physical security monitoring
requirements.text: Monitor physical premises for unauthorized access and suspicious activity. Evidence: camera retention settings, alarm logs, and response records.

requirements.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
requirements.text: Protect facilities from environmental and physical threats such as fire, flood, and power loss. Evidence: risk assessment and protection system test records.

requirements.title: Working in secure areas
requirements.text: Restrict work in secure areas and supervise or escort visitors. Evidence: secure area rules, access lists, and visitor logs.

requirements.title: Clear desk and clear screen
requirements.text: Require staff to secure information and devices when leaving a workspace. Evidence: clear desk policy and spot-check results.

requirements.title: Equipment siting and protection
requirements.text: Site and protect equipment to reduce environmental and unauthorized-access risk. Evidence: equipment placement standards and site inspections.

requirements.title: Security of assets off-premises
requirements.text: Protect assets used outside the premises, including travel and home use. Evidence: off-site asset register and device protection records.

requirements.title: Storage media
requirements.text: Manage storage media through labelling, secure storage, transport, and disposal. Evidence: media register, transfer logs, and destruction certificates.

requirements.title: Supporting utilities
requirements.text: Provide and test supporting utilities that information processing depends on. Evidence: utility inventory, maintenance records, and failover tests.

requirements.title: Cabling security
requirements.text: Protect power and communication cabling from interception, interference, and damage. Evidence: cabling standards and installation inspection records.

requirements.title: Equipment maintenance
requirements.text: Maintain equipment according to manufacturer guidance and record the work. Evidence: maintenance schedule, service reports, and asset history.

requirements.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
requirements.text: Sanitize or destroy equipment and storage media before disposal or reuse. Evidence: disposal procedure and certificates of destruction.

requirements.title: User endpoint devices
requirements.text: Apply configuration and protection standards to user endpoint devices. Evidence: device baseline, compliance reports, and exception list.

requirements.title: Privileged access rights
requirements.text: Limit and monitor privileged access rights, and review them regularly. Evidence: privileged account inventory and review records.

requirements.title: Information access restriction
requirements.text: Restrict access to information and functions according to defined policy. Evidence: access matrix, permission exports, and approvals.

requirements.title: Access to source code
requirements.text: Control read and write access to source code and development artefacts. Evidence: repository permissions and code review records.

requirements.title: Secure authentication
requirements.text: Use secure authentication methods appropriate to the risk, including multi-factor authentication where needed. Evidence: authentication configuration and enforcement reports.

requirements.title: Capacity management
requirements.text: Monitor capacity and plan resources to meet performance and availability needs. Evidence: capacity reports, thresholds, and scaling records.

requirements.title: Protection against malware
requirements.text: Deploy malware protection and keep detection content current. Evidence: endpoint protection console and update compliance reports.

requirements.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
requirements.text: Identify, prioritize, and remediate technical vulnerabilities within defined timelines. Evidence: scan results, patch records, and remediation tickets.

requirements.title: Configuration management
requirements.text: Establish and maintain secure configuration baselines for systems and services. Evidence: hardened images, configuration exports, and drift alerts.

requirements.title: Information deletion
requirements.text: Delete information when it is no longer required and verify deletion where promised. Evidence: retention schedule and deletion records.

requirements.title: Data masking
requirements.text: Mask sensitive data in non-production and lower-trust contexts. Evidence: masking rules and sample test results.

requirements.title: Data leakage prevention
requirements.text: Prevent unauthorized extraction of sensitive information through technical and procedural controls. Evidence: data loss prevention rules, alerts, and investigation records.

requirements.title: Information backup
requirements.text: Back up information and test restoration against agreed objectives. Evidence: backup schedule, restore tests, and failure records.

requirements.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
requirements.text: Provide redundancy for information processing facilities where availability requires it. Evidence: architecture diagram, failover tests, and uptime reports.

requirements.title: Logging
requirements.text: Produce and protect logs that support detection, investigation, and audit. Evidence: logging standard, retention settings, and sample logs.

requirements.title: Monitoring activities
requirements.text: Monitor systems and networks for anomalous behavior and follow up on alerts. Evidence: monitoring dashboards, alert tickets, and tuning records.

requirements.title: Clock synchronization
requirements.text: Synchronize system clocks to an approved time source. Evidence: time source configuration and drift monitoring reports.

requirements.title: Use of privileged utility programs
requirements.text: Restrict and log use of utility programs that can bypass controls. Evidence: utility inventory, approvals, and command logs.

requirements.title: Installation of software on operational systems
requirements.text: Control installation of software on operational systems through approval and verification. Evidence: software catalogue, installation records, and change tickets.

requirements.title: Networks security
requirements.text: Protect networks through segmentation, secure configuration, and monitoring. Evidence: network diagrams, firewall rules, and review records.

requirements.title: Security of network services
requirements.text: Define security requirements for network services and verify that they are met. Evidence: service specifications, configuration baselines, and test results.

requirements.title: Segregation of networks
requirements.text: Separate networks by trust level and business function. Evidence: network zones, segmentation rules, and connectivity tests.

requirements.title: Web filtering
requirements.text: Filter access to external websites to reduce malware and data-loss risk. Evidence: web filter policy and blocked-request reports.

requirements.title: Use of cryptography
requirements.text: Define when and how cryptography is used, including key management. Evidence: cryptography policy, key inventory, and algorithm standards.

requirements.title: Secure development life cycle
requirements.text: Embed security activities into each stage of the development lifecycle. Evidence: development lifecycle definition, security gates, and project records.

requirements.title: Application security requirements
requirements.text: Specify security requirements for applications and verify them before release. Evidence: requirements backlog, threat model, and acceptance tests.

requirements.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
requirements.text: Apply secure architecture and engineering principles to systems and services. Evidence: architecture standards, design reviews, and exceptions.

requirements.title: Secure coding
requirements.text: Set secure coding standards and verify them through review and tooling. Evidence: coding standard, code review records, and scanner results.

requirements.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
requirements.text: Test security in development and acceptance before changes reach production. Evidence: test plans, penetration test reports, and defect records.

requirements.title: Outsourced development
requirements.text: Apply the same security expectations to outsourced development and verify delivery. Evidence: supplier requirements, code review records, and acceptance tests.

requirements.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
requirements.text: Keep development, test, and production environments separated and controlled. Evidence: environment inventory, access controls, and data-flow review.

requirements.title: Change management
requirements.text: Manage changes through request, assessment, approval, testing, and rollback planning. Evidence: change tickets, approvals, and post-implementation reviews.

requirements.title: Test information
requirements.text: Protect test information and prefer synthetic data over production data. Evidence: test data policy and data generation records.

requirements.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
requirements.text: Protect systems and data during audit testing and agree the scope in advance. Evidence: audit plan, access approvals, and test logs.
